title: Radar Outage Snarls O’Hare on Busiest Thanksgiving Travel Day as 17.6 Million Prepare to Fly

content:
A radar outage at Chicago O’Hare International Airport snarled flights on Tuesday, Nov. 24 — the busiest day of what the Federal Aviation Administration calls the busiest Thanksgiving travel week in 16 years.

The FAA said a ground radar system known as ASDE-X, which controllers use to track aircraft and vehicles on runways and taxiways, suffered an outage. The agency first paused most arriving flights into O’Hare, then replaced the ground stop with a ground-delay program while technicians worked on the equipment. The FAA said the problem could last until about 1 a.m. Eastern time on Wednesday.

FlightAware reported about 373 delayed flights at O’Hare, roughly 13 percent of operations at the American Airlines and United Airlines hub, with delays averaging 47 minutes and some aircraft held in the air for up to 30 minutes before landing. Most of the delayed flights — 214 — were headed into Chicago.

The outage landed in the middle of a record holiday rush. The FAA forecast 417,775 flights between Nov. 23 and Dec. 1, with 52,345 flights on Tuesday alone. The Transportation Security Administration expects to screen about 17.6 million passengers over the Thanksgiving week, including more than 3 million on Sunday, Nov. 29, the busiest single day. The TSA is urging travelers to arrive at least two hours early for domestic flights and three hours early for international flights.

The O’Hare failure follows a string of aviation system breakdowns. A telecommunications failure triggered a nationwide FAA ground stop on Nov. 13 that lasted nearly five hours, led to more than 18,000 canceled flights and affected more than 1.5 million passengers. A Delta Air Lines weight-and-balance system outage on Sunday, Nov. 22, delayed roughly 1,300 to 1,600 flights. O’Hare arrivals were also briefly paused on Monday, Nov. 23, because of staffing shortfalls at the local air traffic control facility.

For Laredo families flying out for the holiday, the message from federal officials is the same one they have repeated all week: check flight status before leaving for the airport, and build in extra time. The system is moving record crowds on aging equipment — and this week, that equipment has failed more than once.

Sources: Reuters, Nov. 24, 2026; Federal Aviation Administration; Transportation Security Administration; FlightAware.
